newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $0.50 - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices early Tuesday were steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, but losses could be extended by $1.00 as packers try to mend narrowing operating margins by paying less for hogs, cash dealers said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs traded early at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country, with prices paid at the plant ranging from $57.50 to $58.50, sources there said.

Illinois prices were steady to $0.50 lower, with country values ranging from $55.50 to $56.00 and plants $56.50 to $57.500. Indiana/Ohio country prices ranged from $54.00 to $55.00 and plants from $55.00 to $57.00, sources said.
Packer margins have been pinched recently by a continued erosion of pork prices, dealers and packer buyers said.

Pork values Monday were quoted down $0.54 to $0.57 per cwt on 36 fabricated loads and nine loads of trimmings reported sold, USDA said. Losses were led by declines in hams, pork bellies and lean trimmings.

The weak pork prices offset potential support from perceptions that hog marketings Monday were light and would continue light Tuesday as producers concentrated on getting as much as the harvest finished as possible before rain moves into the Corn Belt later this week.
